groups.title: Seniority & Career Level
groups.finding: Inferred level: Junior. Career-changer from law; retraining completed June 2024 (General Assembly) makes this a recent-graduate profile. Only two UX roles are relevant (contract + internship, total ~1.7 years) — Ashurst legal work is not relevant to UX design despite seniority there. Clearly Junior for a UX/UI Designer target despite impressive prior legal career.
groups.recommendation: Confirm as Junior - this controls tone, assertiveness, and how responsibilities are framed throughout the CV.
groups.insight: Seniority framing is the single biggest lever on how a recruiter reads every bullet.

recommended_overrides.seniority_level: Junior (1.7 relevant / 8.4 total yrs - confirmed by user)

groups.title: Professional Summary - Voice
groups.finding: Your professional summary can be written in first person (you speaking as yourself) or third person (written about you).
examples: First person: "Biomedical Science graduate with hands-on laboratory training…"
Third person: "Sarah is a Biomedical Science graduate with hands-on laboratory training…"
groups.recommendation: Use first person - it reads as direct and modern and is the most common choice today. Prefer third person? Pick "Customise" and type "third person".
groups.insight: First person (or implied first person, with no "I") is standard for most professional summaries; third person can suit very senior or academic profiles.

recommended_overrides.profile_voice: first person - the summary speaks as the candidate (implied first person, no name and no third-person pronouns)
